cands.bio: U.S. Representative for Alabama's 7th District since 2011. Securities and public finance lawyer before Congress, including at Davis Polk & Wardwell and Maynard, Cooper & Gale, where she was the first Black woman partner. Serves on the Ways and Means Committee. Princeton, Oxford and Harvard Law graduate.

endorsements.text: The Professional Fire Fighters of Alabama endorsed Sewell for re-election, according to her campaign site.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from Terri Sewell on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land purchases, slowing development, state or local growth policy, school vouchers or charters, or teacher pay. We found no record of her position on red-flag laws, gun purchase-age limits or suppressors, or on police pay and pensions or penalties for public disorder. We also found no documented stance on H-1B visas or state contracts. The Ballotpedia page was cut off partway through the 118th Congress key votes, so later items on it were not read. Ballotpedia says she did not complete its candidate survey. Her campaign site lists her issues but gives no detail on these topics.

votes.what: Final FY2026 spending package funding most remaining federal agencies through September 30, 2026.

votes.bill: S. 1071 / FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act (final)
votes.what: Final FY2026 defense policy and funding-authorization bill (about $900 billion), carried in the House on the vehicle S. 1071.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Nov. 12 final, ended the shutdown)
votes.what: Ended the 43-day federal shutdown: funds government through Jan. 30, 2026 and three full-year spending bills.

votes.bill: H.R. 5371 (2025) Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2026 (Sept. 19 House passage)
votes.what: House-passed stopgap funding bill to keep government open through Nov. 21, 2025; stalled in the Senate and a shutdown began Oct. 1.

votes.bill: H.R. 1 (2025) One Big Beautiful Bill Act (final passage)
votes.what: The 2025 reconciliation law: extends the 2017 tax cuts, adds new tax breaks, cuts Medicaid and food-assistance spending, and raises defense and border spending and the debt limit.

votes.bill: H.R. 881 (2025) DHS Restrictions on Confucius Institutes and Chinese Entities of Concern Act
votes.what: Bars Homeland Security funds going to Confucius Institutes and entities tied to the Chinese government.
Requires documentary proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

votes.bill: H.R. 1968 (2025) Full-Year Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2025
votes.what: Funds the federal government through September 30, 2025 at roughly prior-year levels (March 2025 stopgap).

votes.bill: H.R. 152 (2025) Federal Disaster Assistance Coordination Act
votes.what: Streamlines coordination among federal agencies delivering disaster aid (hurricane/flood recovery).
Requires federal detention of undocumented immigrants charged with theft, burglary or assault of a police officer, and lets states sue over immigration enforcement.

money.note: Individuals gave $162,462; PAC money $8,000; candidate's own money $100,000. Percentages describe itemized individual gifts, which the FEC has processed through about July 2026.

cands.bio: Entrepreneur and educator who has worked as a teacher, principal and college educator. She co-founded a shared nonprofit facility and is developing Hub in the Hills, a nonprofit campus in a former elementary school. Republican nominee for Alabama's 7th Congressional District in 2026. She has held no public office.
cands.gaps: We found no stated positions from Akin on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, guns, abortion, or school vouchers and charters. Her site's education plank speaks only of cooperation among teachers, parents and communities. She has held no office, so there is no official record of actions. We could not find where she was born or raised, or when she came to Alabama. Her site gives no dates for her jobs, and its career details are self-reported. We found no endorsements, controversies or foreign ties. She did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey.
